verdict: Disney's revenue rose 6% to $22.6B and segment profit jumped 23% as streaming turned profitable — but $1.5B of impairment charges held reported EPS to $0.25, versus $1.14 excluding those items.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,067M, Sports $929M, Experiences $1,659M (before corporate costs).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Writing down assets that lost value — goodwill at the general entertainment networks, retail stores, Star India and content (detailed below).

follow100Note: Of the $2.50 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.46 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $2.04 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Segment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Total segment operating income rose 23% to $3.7B: Entertainment more than quadrupled to $1,067M as streaming swung to a profit and Inside Out 2 and Deadpool & Wolverine powered content sales, while Experiences eased 6% to $1,659M on softer international park attendance.

takeaways.title: Streaming turned the corner
takeaways.text: Entertainment's Direct-to-Consumer business earned $253M versus a $420M loss a year ago, on revenue up 15% to $5.8B; Disney's combined streaming businesses made $321M. Linear networks went the other way — operating income fell 38% to $498M.

takeaways.title: Charges masked the progress
takeaways.text: Reported EPS was just $0.25 because the quarter absorbed $1,543M of restructuring and impairment charges. Excluding such items, adjusted EPS rose 39% to $1.14.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $1,543M — impairments of goodwill ($584M, at the general entertainment linear networks), retail assets ($328M), Star India ($210M), content ($187M) and equity investments ($165M), plus $69M of severance.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $361M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $107M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
footerNote: Of the $564M of net income, $104M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $460M is attributable to Disney (the $0.25 EPS figure). Costs are split between services and products using the fiscal 2024 10-K less the first nine months reported in the Q3 FY24 10-Q, since the earnings release reports one combined cost line; operating income of $1,202M is derived as revenue less those costs and the restructuring charge.
